newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico soybean 96-97 imports seen over 2.8 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Mexico soybean 96-97 imports seen over 2.8 mln T.

text.p: Mexican soybean imports in the 1996-1997 cycle will likely be slightly higher than the estimated 2.7 million tonnes in the 1995-1996 cycle, the American Soybean Association's local office said Friday.
"Unconfirmed reports indicate there were 400,000 tonnes of purchases in the last two weeks," the association said in an update.
"At that rate, the calendar year imports will top the 2.8 million tonne level," the office said, adding out the soybean calendar year runs from September 1 to August 31.
"Again this is highly dependent on the price of the peso," it added, pointing out foreign exchange fluctuations are a determining import factor for commodities.

To October 24, soybean imports from the United States totaled 265,700 tonnes, the association said, giving latest concrete data available, although not considering many of the unconfirmed reports of the recent import surge.
That confirmed figure compares to the 292,200 tonnes imported by Mexico from the United States to October 19, 1995, the nearest comparative date available.
The United States provides Mexico with around 95 percent of its soybean import needs, the other trickle coming usually from other Latin nations, such as Brazil or Argentina.
